newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LIFTS CUSTOMS DUTY ON IMPORTED HARVESTERS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LIFTS CUSTOMS DUTY ON IMPORTED HARVESTERS.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Monday suspended customs duties levied on imported grain harvesting machines until end-1997 in a bid to upgrade its outdated harvesting equipment and help collect this year's crop.

"No customs duties and fees will be levied on imported harvesting machines until the end of the year according to today's cabinet decision," Farm Minister Ventsislav Varbanov told repoters after a cabinet session.
The decree, will be come into force after being published in the State Gazette.
Custom duties and fees levied on imported harvesters amounted to between 50,000 and 100,000 German marks, which was unaffordable for wheat producers, Varbanov said.

In April the interim cabinet approved a future contract to import eight combine harvesters from Germany against export of 5,000 tonnes of wheat for this year's crop in a bid to improve the harvesting capability of Bulgaria's outdated mashinery.

Bulgaria has only 6,600 outdated combine harvesters at present, and this year's crop was expected to last 90 days instead of the usual 30 days due to shortage of of combine harvesters, the agriculture ministry figures said.

The reformist government freed grain prices and trade earlier this year to encourage local grain producers and avoid repetition of grain crises. Uncontrolled exports two years ago led to unprecedented bread shortages in the beginning of this year.
